clue.text: During which heads are almost sure to roll?

definitions.text: During which heads are almost sure to roll?

parts.words: During which heads are almost sure to roll?
parts.note: reads like a grim prophecy of executions, but describes an acrobatic move in which the head goes over and round

explanation.surface: A dark forecast that a purge or revolution is bound to see people beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads roll' suggests sackings or the guillotine; here the gymnast's own head literally rolls over as the body turns heels over head.
explanation.definitionFit: In this acrobatic flip the body turns a full circle, so the head rolls over the ground or through the air.

clue.text: The twins, say, communicate non — verbally

definitions.meaning: Gemini, the twins, is an example of a zodiac ...

explanation.surface: Twins talk to each other without words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a star sign of the zodiac; and to sign is to gesture rather than speak.

clue.text: Intended to finish early, being tight

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: meant ... intended

explanation.surface: A miser planned to leave early, being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean and tight both describe someone unwilling to spend money.

clue.text: Drafts in hooligans

explanation.surface: Thugs are being conscripted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drafts' suggests call-up; here it means preliminary versions. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough drafts are preliminary sketches; and roughs are ruffians.

clue.text: Hating cereal is not ones' inclination

explanation.surface: Disliking breakfast cereal isn't what one naturally feels.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from woodworking: cutting across the wood's fibres, hence contrary to someone's nature; read literally it is opposing grain.

clue.text: Hide in bed, listening

indicators.note: while listening, the bed word is heard as a phrase spelt differently

parts.note: a Lilo is an inflatable air bed

explanation.surface: Someone hides under the covers, eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lilo is a British brand of inflatable mattress used at the beach or camping. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to keep out of sight, an idiom for hiding.

clue.text: Old president's got time to help

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a former US president

explanation.surface: A former head of state has found a moment to lend assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, a synonym of help.

clue.text: Paper's bad — so there are misprints

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: misprinted letters are set in the wrong places, so these are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a newspaper is poor, riddled with typos.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper.

clue.text: Illegally entered resorts in the Sahara on the way back

indicators.note: the resorts sit inside the desert word
the word for the Sahara is read in the return direction

parts.note: the Sahara is a desert
spas are health resorts

explanation.surface: Someone broke in at desert resorts on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the desert is turned round by 'on the way back'; the resorts read forwards inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go onto property without permission.

clue.text: Like sugar could be cultivated in Tuareg land!

indicators.note: land that is cultivated is worked over and turned, so these letters are tilled into a new order

explanation.surface: Sugar cane might be grown in the desert country of the Tuareg nomads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges the ten letters of TUAREG LAND. The Tuareg are a Saharan people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary table sugar comes as small crystals, described as granulated.

clue.text: When speaking recognizes the bouquet

indicators.note: signals that a word spoken out loud is heard as another with a different spelling

parts.note: to recognize something is to know it, so recognizes gives knows

explanation.surface: A wine buff spots the aroma of a vintage just by talking about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its aroma or bouquet, a tasting term.

clue.text: Sport of kings? Cite a new development

indicators.note: a development makes something new of these letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Horse racing is the sport of kings; perhaps a new trend is emerging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport of kings' is a stock phrase for horse racing; here 'of' is a link and 'kings' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skating is a winter sport on frozen surfaces.

clue.text: Almost the first time I have the energy and resourcefulness

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, missing its last letter

parts.note: initial means first
I've contracts I have

explanation.surface: Almost the first time someone shows drive and enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiative is enterprise: the drive to start things without prompting.

clue.text: Apparition of a cat chasing loud, enthusiastic follower

indicators.note: the cat runs behind, so its piece comes after
said loud, out in the open air, so the follower word is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiastic follower
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A ghostly creature appears as a cat hunts down a noisy, keen supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud' looks like an adjective on the follower, but signals a sound-alike spelling; 'chasing' puts the cat second. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost or spectre, an apparition that seems to appear.

clue.text: Fraught with danger — poor soul even on top

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above comes first

parts.note: par means equal or even

indicators.note: poor means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wretched person is in danger even when apparently successful.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous means perilous, full of risk.

clue.text: Copying two identical notes on blubber

indicators.note: the note is given twice over

parts.note: mi is a note in the sol-fa scale
to blubber is to cry

explanation.surface: Two matching notes written about whale fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue it puts MIMI above CRY. 'blubber' looks like whale fat; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation of another's manner or appearance.

clue.text: Lots of line-dancing

parts.note: reads as a lot of dancing in lines, but means several instances of one particular Latin-American line dance

explanation.surface: A dance hall full of people moving in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a dance in which people form a long single-file line, so many such dances are plural.

clue.text: Close down when gale is blowing

definitions.meaning: to bring a business or affair to an end
a description of the wind being up, a strong breeze rising

explanation.surface: A business shuts its doors as a storm blows in.
explanation.definitionFit: To end operations is idiomatically to wind things up; and the wind is up when a gale blows.

clue.text: Receptors of food served in space?

definitions.meaning: playful reading of plates of food orbiting the Earth

explanation.surface: Astronauts' meals delivered in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish aerials receive broadcasts from orbiting transmitters; and dishes of food aboard an orbiting craft would be the same words read literally.

clue.text: It might work out a bill in public transport

indicators.note: the bill sits inside the transport word

parts.note: a bus is public transport
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone tots up the fare on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like money owed for the fare; as wordplay it is AC, short for account. 'It might work out' needs no object: a calculating frame works sums out.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of sliding beads used for calculating, so it could total a bill.

clue.text: Safeguard pawn

explanation.surface: Protect the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a guarantee; and a pawn is a pledge or security left with a lender.

clue.text: Country church by the common, unfinished

indicators.note: the common's word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a village common is a green
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rural church stands beside the village common, its building incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective on church, but is the definition; 'by' simply places the church after the shortened common.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Where fires start raging in exits

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the exits word

parts.note: gates are exits

indicators.note: the opening letter of raging

explanation.surface: Where fires begin blazing at the exits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start raging' suggests fires flaring up; 'start' takes R from 'raging'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grates are fireplace frames where fires are laid and burn.

clue.text: Press tracks the operating procedure

parts.note: a surge of a crowd is a press or crush forward
RY is short for railway, which runs on tracks

explanation.surface: Journalists follow up on how a company works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists; it is a rush forward. 'tracks' looks like a verb but gives the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is medical treatment by operation.

clue.text: Flower that's satirised, to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the word satirised is taken, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A bloom that's been mocked in some lampoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms.

clue.text: Sources of energy topped up in case

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Batteries recharged inside their casing.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Poems included in "a modest proposal"

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Verses within Swift's satirical essay A Modest Proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Chester was once said to be in ruins

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for Chester, an English city
stated means said

explanation.surface: Chester was supposedly once a ruined city.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is a city in north-west England, called Deva by the Romans. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastated means laid waste, wrecked, utterly destroyed.

clue.text: Delight at finding good shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to find a decent refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great happiness or joy.

clue.text: Mystic sang about sporting exercise

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A mystic chanted on the subject of physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastics is physical training in agility and strength, practised as a sport.
